name: Emotet delivery chain — incident summary
content:
## Summary

A phishing wave delivered **Emotet** to three staff mailboxes between 09:10 and
11:40 UTC. Two recipients opened the attachment; one host reached the C2 before
the address was blocked at the perimeter. No data staging or lateral movement
was observed.

## Delivery

The lure was an invoice-themed Word document, `invoice_48812.doc`, sent from a
lookalike billing domain. The macro fetches a loader from a compromised
WordPress host and writes it to `%APPDATA%`.

| Stage | Indicator |
|---|---|
| Lure | `invoice_48812.doc` |
| Loader URL | `http://invoice-portal.test/download/48812` |
| C2 | `185.220.101.42` |

## Why this matters

`185.220.101.42` is the same address seen in the Cobalt Strike campaign against
EU banks two weeks earlier. The correlation was not made by an analyst — the
platform surfaced it when the second event was submitted. Whether the two are
the same operator or a shared bulletproof host is unresolved; see the opinion
attached to the Cobalt Strike event.

## Actions taken

1. Blocked the C2 address at the perimeter and the sending domain at the gateway.
2. Reimaged the one host that completed the callback.
3. Pushed the loader URL and document hash to the detection pipeline.

## Open questions

- The loader host is a legitimate site that was compromised; the owner has not
  responded to notification.
- Only two of the three recipients have been interviewed.

> Analyst note: treat the TA542 attribution as provisional. It rests on the
> delivery chain resembling previous Emotet waves, not on infrastructure the
> group is known to own.
